what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It helps control symptoms like tremors (shaking), stiffness, and slow movements. It works by increasing the amount of dopamine in your brain, which is a chemical your body needs for smooth, controlled movement. Entacapone helps levodopa work longer and more effectively.
how_to_take: Take this tablet by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Do not take more than one tablet at each dose. If you are switching from regular carbidopa/levodopa, your doctor will decide the right strength for you. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose and schedule that is right for you. Most people take this medicine several times a day, spread evenly throughout the day. Common strengths include Stalevo 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, and 200. Never take extra tablets to make up for a missed dose, and never change your dose on your own. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never double up on doses to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine with a high-protein meal or high-protein diet, as protein can reduce how well levodopa works. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase side effects like dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Be careful when driving or operating machinery until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause sudden sleepiness. Avoid taking iron supplements or antacids containing iron at the same time as this medicine, as they can lower the amount of medicine absorbed by your body. Let all your doctors and dentists know you are taking this medicine before any procedures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: uncontrollable movements of your face, arms, or legs (called dyskinesia); a sudden high fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, or fast heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); unusual urges such as gambling, increased sexual urges, or compulsive eating or spending; severe diarrhea; fainting or very low blood pressure; hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); sudden daytime sleepiness or falling asleep without warning; dark, brown, or black urine (this can be normal with entacapone but check with your doctor); chest pain or irregular heartbeat; depression or thoughts of self-harm; or allergic reactions such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your Parkinson's symptoms within a few days to weeks, but it can take several weeks to get the full benefit. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time to find the best level for you. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well. Do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: This medicine is commonly used in older adults but may cause more dizziness, confusion, or falls. Use extra caution. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known. Breastfeeding: It is not recommended to breastfeed while taking this medicine. Talk to your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
